claims.text: Random compositional fluctuations in single-phase multi-component concentrated alloys produce severe lattice distortions.
Severe lattice distortions perturb equilibrium edge-dislocation core structures and make them non-planar or wavy.
Non-planar edge-dislocation cores have reduced mobility.
Reduced dislocation mobility is the primary cause of enhanced yield strength and altered deformation behavior relative to lower-distortion alloys.
NbTaTiV is a single-phase BCC refractory high-entropy alloy.
NbTaTiV has a random elemental distribution involving elements with different atomic radii.
Substituting elements with alternatives of more similar atomic radii can reduce effective lattice distortion while leaving electron concentration and phase stability substantially unchanged.
NbTaTiV remains a single BCC solid solution through mechanical testing at temperatures up to 900°C.
NbTaTiV can be studied by in situ neutron diffraction during compression at room temperature, 500°C, 700°C, and 900°C.
Wavy edge-dislocation cores are the structural mediator that impedes dislocation glide.
Atomic-size disorder shifts dislocation-core positions away from their neutral planes.
Departure from a planar dislocation core increases the energy barrier for dislocation motion.
Increasing the barrier to dislocation motion raises yield stress and alters the plastic-deformation mechanism.
An alloy with greater atomic-size mismatch will have higher yield strength than the reduced-distortion baseline.
An alloy with greater atomic-size mismatch will have lower dislocation mobility than the reduced-distortion baseline.
The high-distortion alloy will exhibit a greater prevalence of wavy or disturbed dislocation cores than the baseline.
The proposed mechanism should apply when the alloys are single-phase and dislocation motion is the rate-limiting deformation process.
Secondary phases or processing-induced grain-boundary phases can make other deformation mechanisms dominate.
The quantitative relationship between lattice distortion and yield-strength enhancement is not established.
The cited NbTaTiV alloy has a yield strength of 1064 MPa at room temperature and 595 MPa at 900°C.

contradictions.description: The intervention requires elemental substitutions to change atomic-size variance, whereas the falsification design says that the two alloy sets have identical overall compositions. Distinct substitutional chemistries cannot also be compositionally identical.

The prediction says the high-distortion alloy should have reduced dislocation mobility, but the falsification rule treats failure of its dislocation mobility to significantly exceed the baseline as falsifying. Non-exceeding mobility is consistent with, rather than contrary to, the stated prediction.
